themes.name: Click 9.0, deprecations and internal API cleanup

duplicates.reason: Both report that usage-line wrapping (textwrap break_on_hyphens) splits hyphenated metavars/options across lines at the dash.
Both request appending '...' to the metavar of multiple=True options in help output to show the option can be repeated.

top_issues.reason: Click 9.0 release tracking issue; it coordinates the deprecation removals and breaking changes.
Confirmed help-output bug with a clear reproduction and identified cause (break_on_hyphens); also reported again as 90101.
click.edit fails on Windows about half the time; needs a maintainer to decide whether it is a Click bug or a Windows platform issue.
Removing deprecated code is a prerequisite for the 9.0 release.
Long-standing help-text newline problem with an identified code location and a proposed fix in 3016.

records.judge_reason: Most labelled themes are recognisable in the report: help formatting, help customisation, Click 9.0 and types/parameters. There are several problems, though. #3022 (FORCE_COLOR/NO_COLOR) is placed in help formatting rather than terminal utilities. #2875 (prompt building) sits under types. #2917 (e2e completion testing) is lumped into terminal utilities, which makes that theme a mixed bag. #3094 is duplicated across two themes, and #3696 is duplicated across documentation and 9.0. The terminal utilities theme is weakened as a result. Overall it is mostly the labelled structure, but with several misplacements and overlaps.

duplicates.reason: Both report that a click.File(lazy=True) default still fails at startup with 'No such file or directory' when the file is missing, even though it is never opened.

top_issues.reason: Bug: completing a long option written as --opt=value loses the option name in zsh and offers nothing in bash. The issue gives clear steps to reproduce.
Bug on current click 8.5.0: lazy=True does not stop the missing-file check for a File default. It is the same problem as 2429, which has been open a long time.
Bug: get_parameter_source returns None under ctx.invoke and ctx.forward. Other users have run into it, including dbt.
Bug: default callbacks run during tab completion, which slows completion down. The resilient_parsing docs no longer match what the code does.
Requested feature: let negative numbers be parsed as arguments. Users call it critical; it should be planned together with the parser meta issue 2834.

records.judge_reason: The report has no separate errors/exceptions theme. #2740 and #2419 go under help/styling, which is defensible, but #2853 (exception call stack) is misplaced in shell completion. Splitting file/lazy handling into its own theme is coherent. The parser theme picks up #2402 and #2801, which are command invocation issues and arguably misplaced. The Click 9 / internals theme is dissolved: #2493 and #2823 go to context, which is a reasonable fit for #2493, and #2706 (i18n) goes to help output. Most groupings are reasonable, with a few misplacements, one clearly wrong.

themes.name: Parameter types, file handling and testing

duplicates.reason: Both report that with chain=True, an option placed after a subcommand's argument is rejected (No such option/command), even though the chaining docs say chained commands accept options and arguments as normal.
Both report that confirm prompts read from piped stdin instead of the terminal, and both ask for prompts to read from the tty.

top_issues.reason: Long-standing chaining bug where the behaviour contradicts the docs; reported again in #90121 on click 8.5.0, so users are still hitting it.
Shell completion callbacks get a context without ctx.obj, which causes an AttributeError; the maintainer has said they would review a PR.
Completion callbacks can't see already-parsed argument values in ctx.params, which breaks context-aware completion.
Most-discussed feature request (23 comments) for basic async support, with a related request in #2360.
Planned parser rewrite that underlies many open parsing issues (#590, #1322, #742, #730).

records.judge_reason: The report regroups the issues reasonably, and most groupings hold together. Shell completion matches the labelled theme, plus #1574 (context.params access), which is a defensible move. Async gets its own theme, which is coherent. Prompts/stdin matches the terminal I/O theme apart from #1997. The help formatting theme merges help customisation with #944 (exception colour), which is plausible. The parser theme is broad: it puts the parser rewrites together with the chaining and subcommand issues, and adds #531, which is reasonable since the labelled themes split these across commands and parsing. The weak spot is the last theme, which mixes param types and file handling with #1997 (testing output width), an unrelated issue. Overall the groupings are mostly coherent with a few misplacements, and the parser theme is overly large.
